statement: When matching was within a range (a matching factor differs within some sets), conditional logistic regression does not remove what the matching left, which may confound a little.
regime: individually matched sets with a range-matched factor

statement: The specification curve must not be fitted or shown before the analysis plan is locked: seeing specification estimates first would invite choosing the plan by its estimate (Gelman & Loken's forking paths).
regime: Estimate an effect; recorded choices with declared alternatives
decision: specification curve (Which of my decisions mattered?), after the lock
claimed_basis: calm/FOUNDATION §5 rule 6; Gelman & Loken 2013; BLUEPRINT §11 (after the lock)

statement: A reliability estimated from internal consistency (α or ω) omits transient (occasion-specific) error, so a correction based on it under-corrects, whereas a test-retest repeat administration includes transient error.
decision: label on corrections from internal consistency; ranking of test-retest above ω
claimed_basis: Schmidt, Le & Ilies 2003 (Psychol Methods 8:206); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 8

statement: Adjusting for total energy does not by itself make a substitution isocaloric: the swapped components must be measured and analyzed in calories, and with components in grams or servings the substitution reported is not the one intended.
regime: dietary lens; substitution between two exposures
decision: whether a substitution is offered (two energy-bearing exposures required) and its unit

statement: An energy source's amounts are settled as grams by the Atwater identity only where it excludes every other unit: the identity passes (ratio 0.90-1.10) with the column read in grams, the column is not alcohol (standard drinks hold 8-20 g by country and alcohol is a minor source), the column carries at least 1 - 1/1.10 (about 9%) of reconstructed energy on the median row (below that any unit, or none, keeps the ratio in band), and reading it in kg, kcal or kJ instead moves the ratio out of band; otherwise a substitution or partition waits for the user's recorded unit.
regime: Dietary substitution / partition energy models; macronutrient energy sources.
decision: kcal per unit used to move energy through a source in substitution and partition models.
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.3 (sixth gate: US standard drinks reconstructed at 1.02 read as grams; an InBody Protein confirmed in kg moved energy at 4 kcal per unit); Kalinowski & Humphreys 2016 Addiction 111:1293 (8-20 g); NUTRITION_PACK §01.

statement: For internal validation at typical clinical sample sizes, a single random 70/30 train/test split is the recommended default, because it gives a less biased and more precise estimate of performance than bootstrap optimism correction or repeated cross-validation.
regime: internal validation at typical clinical sample sizes (hundreds to a few thousand rows)
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A5.5 (CONVENTION); Steyerberg et al. 2001 (J Clin Epidemiol 54:774).

statement: Under a population survey design, a subgroup analysis should first delete the rows outside the subgroup and then compute Taylor-linearized variances, because keeping them would let PSUs with no subgroup members inflate the subgroup's standard error.
regime: population survey design (strata, PSUs), subgroup analysis
decision: subgroup analysis under a survey design

statement: A proportional-hazards failure of the exposure is declared when the cox.zph score test of the exposure's own term (not the global test or the covariates' terms) has p < 0.05, the customary level; the failure then carries response exits.
decision: whether the PH check is 'failed' and response exits are offered
claimed_basis: PH_ALPHA = 0.05 'at the customary level' (turbotab/core/models/effects.py:88); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11

statement: The precision of a held-out AUC is approximated by Hanley & McNeil's (1982) standard error at an assumed AUC of 0.75 for the held-out events and non-events, and the precision of a held-out macro-F1 by a proportion's worst-case 95% interval (±1.96·√(0.25/k)) on the rarest class's k held-out rows.
regime: binary or multiclass outcome; split question before any fit
decision: The precision shown beside each holdout size
claimed_basis: Hanley & McNeil 1982, Radiology 143:29–36 for the AUC; none stated for the macro-F1 approximation.

statement: For a numeric exposure, a cross-fitted R² of 0.9 or more of the exposure on the covariates (a variance inflation factor of 10) is a practical positivity violation: the effect rests on little of the exposure's own variation and extrapolates where it does not vary, so the estimate is refused until every row is kept on the record.
regime: inference; numeric exposure; DML-PLR or PDS
claimed_basis: Kutner, Nachtsheim & Neter 2004 §10.5 (VIF 10, 'the conventional line'); the app's convention

statement: When a time-varying confounder was itself affected by earlier exposure, standard regression is biased whether it adjusts for that confounder or not, while marginal structural models with inverse-probability weights or the parametric g-formula adjust for it at each time point; stabilized weights should average near 1.
regime: inference; exposure varying within units over time points

statement: In a nutrition exposure–outcome analysis, any covariate associated with both the exposure and the outcome in the data, including BMI and blood pressure measured at the same visit, belongs in the adjustment set as a confounder, since association with both is the criterion for confounding.
regime: nutrition exposure–outcome analysis, cross-sectional or cohort

statement: Under inference with repeated units at or above the unit floor, GEE with an exchangeable working correlation and CR2 (bias-reduced linearization) intervals on Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom gives near-nominal type I error even with about 12 units, and below the unit floor its intervals are refused with the mixed model as the exit.
regime: Inference; continuous or binary outcome; repeated units
decision: GEE table intervals, refusal below the floor, and its shelf score
claimed_basis: Liang & Zeger 1986; McCaffrey & Bell, Stat Med 2006;25:4081 (BRL); unit floor = seal.min_groups() = 8 (utils/test_lockbox.py:70).
